transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Park. I wanted to come by and talk to you about your scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was some of an issue with how we did the test.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An issue? What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We used a special dye for the images, but we should have checked your blood levels more carefully first. There was some confusion with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. What is the dye?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is the contrast agent. It helps us see the organs. But for some people, it can be hard on the kidneys.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My kidneys? Are they sick now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is possible. Your blood test showed your kidneys were already a bit weak, and the dye might make that worse.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I feel... I am very worried. I am alone here and I do not know—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion about the process, but we were really busy in the radiology department today and the check was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did you do it if it is dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a mistake in the flow of the department.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I am scared. I do not know what to do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the main thing is that we are watching you now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I be okay? I need to go back to school soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how the numbers look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more medicine? Or a different doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just going to keep an eye on your urine output.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what that means. Urine output?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: How much you pee.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Is that... is that a problem?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to make sure your kidneys are still working.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very strange. I think I want to call my father.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is fine, but I really have to go check on another patient right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, can you tell me if this is my fault? Did I tell you wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it wasn't your fault. Things just didn't go quite right with the timing of the blood work review.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? When do I know if I am sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably do another blood test tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Then we'll see where we are.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very confused. I don't understand why this happened if it was in my chart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was some confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the hospital help me if I get more sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are taking care of you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I don't know my rights here. I am just a student.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You don't need to worry about that. We are just monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am shaking. I am very nervous.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Let's just focus on the fluids for now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Am I in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't think so, but we have to wait for the tests.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did the other nurse say you would be here longer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure. Let's wrap this up for now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please, I just want to know if my kidney is broken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's not broken, it's just stressed. We will check it again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll stay tuned for the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will you come back?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you tell me exactly what the number is?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how it goes. I have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you doctor.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I really have to go', 'Let's wrap this up for now', 'I have to go now').

E.justification: The error is named, but there are no comprehension checks and the resident uses medical jargon ('contrast agent') without checking if the patient understands.

A.justification: The resident says 'I am sorry', but immediately dilutes it with an excuse about the department being 'really busy'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but does not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague steps ('we'll see where we are', 'stay tuned') with no patient role or prevention plan.
